To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beige locus (bg) and the pearl locus (pe) are closely linked and are located between the histone gene (hist1) and the prolactin locus (prl) on mouse chromosome 12.

the genes encoding the prolactin and T-cell receptor gamma chain proteins are linked to the beige locus, and that the genes encoding histone, Friend virus integration site 2 and the dihydrofolic acid reductase are linked to the pearl locus
the linkage map of chromosome 13 has been extended and refined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the genes responsible, in mice, for two human pigment disorders, Chediak- Higashi syndrome and the Hermansky-Puddlak syndrome.
mapping the genes responsible for human pigmentary disorders.
mapping the genetic loci responsible for the two pigment mutations bg and pe on the 13th mouse chromosome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the beige and pearl mutations on mouse chromosome are linked to the Tcrg, Hist1, Prl, Fim-1, Muhf/Ct1a-3 and Dhfr loci in the order: bg-Tcrg-Hist1-Prl-Fim-1-Muhf/Ctta-3-Dhfr-pe, with a total map distance of approximately 20 cM between the bg and the pe loci.

bg is linked to Tcrg, Hist1, Prl, Fim-1, Muhf/CtLa-3 and Dhfr, and pe is linked to Tcrb, Tcrd and Tcrg, and that the linkage group for bg is located at 13.2 centimorgan from the centromere, whereas that for pe is 13.3 centimorgans from the centromeric end of chromosome 13.
the bg locus is 2.0 +/- 0.4 cM from Tcrg, 2.0 cM from Hist1, 2.4 cM (2.0 +/-0.5) from Muhf/Ctia-3 and 2.0 (+/- 1.0) cM from Prl, while pe is located 2.0 (1.0 +/- 1.0 cM) from Fim-1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have defined linkage relationships between multiple loci and two pigment mutations on the distal end of mouse chromosome 13.
the linkage map for mouse chromosome 13 has been extended by the addition of the loci Tcrg, Hist1, Prl, Fim-1, Muhf/Ct1-3 and Dhfr.
the bg and pe mutations on chromosome 13 are closely linked to the Tcrg, Muhf/Ct1a-3 and Prl loci and distal from the Hist1 locus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use these markers to map the genes that cause Chediak-Hagashi and Hermansky Pudlak syndromes.
the beige gene is located on mouse chromosome 11 and that the pearl gene is located on chromosome 13, and that both genes are associated with other genes that are also located on those chromosomes.
the linkage of the two pigment mutations to each other, to Tcrg and to the other loci is consistent with the linkage reported previously for bg, but not for pe.
